operation: GegenNet obtains structural spectral node features from signed TRAIN topology, then applies separate positive/negative polynomial graph filters plus an identity channel at each layer, concatenates/transforms the three outputs, and scores bipartite pairs with a two-layer MLP trained by sign BCE.
relationship_to_current_work: Signed graph-specific filters, three-channel structural fusion, polynomial basis design and spectral initialization are explicit prior operations. A GNNM adaptation using this backbone would establish portability only until an additional predictive and distinguishable method is supported. This source does not describe the current shared NCNC private completion bank or the frozen J/F observation-pattern supervision in the scoped method, which is not global novelty clearance.
distinct_dataset_lead: Signed bipartite link-sign prediction uses observed positive and negative interactions, unlike unobserved Collab TRAIN incidences. It is a possible complementary task where masked row-pattern supervision has known sign labels. No scientific pilot is admitted from this read.
possible_extension_for_further_design: A future bounded hypothesis could compare query/user-wide observed-sign-pattern supervision with equally supervised marginal sign supervision in a shared modern signed-graph model. Keep every training-only adjacency/initializer input identical and test whether any benefit survives capable same-context structured single controls. Mixture-of-Bernoulli pattern likelihood remains GRAN ancestry.
important_limits: A positive/negative/identity route mixture and spectral initialization cannot be claimed as new from this paper.
Training signed adjacency and spectral features must be rebuilt from FIT observations only. The scoped reading does not authenticate the author code split or label-leakage policy.
Published benchmark claims in the abstract are author-reported, not current-project results or an independently reproduced state-of-the-art comparison.
No empirical failure of a current unsigned initialization study refutes all signed graph variants.
The exact mathematical equations and coefficients should be checked against author code before implementation. No numerical basis or theorem verification was performed.
Signed link-sign classification has a recommendation context but is not a measured top-K recommendation task.
